title: Predictive Cognition, Simulation & Decision Intelligence
summary: Gives FRIDAY the ability to think before acting. Before any significant action the Simulation Brain generates multiple scenarios, predicts outcomes (with confidence), forecasts resource/time cost, scores quantitative risk across eight dimensions, evaluates + ranks candidate plans, and recommends the safest. It ADVISES the Executive Brain — it never executes. Only meaningful simulations are persisted (via the Memory Brain), and actual outcomes feed back so prediction accuracy improves. Additive on the M18 brain framework + M16 services; lives under core/brains/simulation/ (distinct from the M11 core/simulation engine).
objective: Observe -> Understand -> Predict -> Simulate -> Compare -> Evaluate Risk -> Select Best Plan -> Execute -> Learn. FRIDAY never blindly executes important actions.
pipeline: SimulationRequest -> scenario generation -> prediction -> forecast -> risk scoring -> decision evaluation -> ranking -> recommended (safest) plan -> (Executive decides) -> learning feedback

components.scenario_generator: multiple candidate futures (immediate / backup-then / ask-user / dry-run; redact; cautious / deferred); rule-based + extensible
components.predictor: intent, next actions, success probability, completion, failure modes (+ confidence); calibrated by learning feedback
components.decision_evaluator: expected success/time/cost/resource, risk level, confidence, dependencies, policy compliance, reasoning, composite score (config-weighted)
components.history: store only meaningful sims (success/repeated-failure/frequently-selected/high-value) via Memory Brain; learning feedback (predicted vs actual)
components.simulation: SimulationBrain orchestrator (Cognitive Brain; never executes; advises only)

executive_integration.flow: Situation -> Simulation Request -> Scenario Generation -> Risk Analysis -> Plan Ranking -> Executive Decision -> Execution -> ExecutiveBrain.report_outcome (learning)
executive_integration.rule: the Executive remains responsible for the final decision; the Simulation Brain only advises; rejected (all plans too risky) -> ask_user

performance: incremental simulation (stops at the timeout budget)
public_api: simulate(action, context?, options?) -> ranked plans + recommended (advisory)
invariants: the Simulation Brain never executes actions (advisory only)
the Executive Brain makes the final decision (not bypassed)
memory is written only through the Memory Brain (not bypassed); only meaningful sims persist
communication only via services + the Runtime event bus + situation reports
never-raises; thread-safe; configuration-driven; no hardcoded values
no circular imports; no side effects at import
